source: Direct user clarification in project chat
raw_user_statement: One thing I should mention, the measurements done on the inner plate WERE within a single plane. They're likely very very accurate. Make sure that difference is noted.
scope: Previously supplied inner-plate face dimensions, not the separately reported foam/assembly depth measurements or the installed projection tip distances.
measurement_plane: A single plane on the loose inner plate, confirmed by the user.
confidence: Owner considers the inner-plate caliper readings highly accurate. Use direct measured dimensions ahead of scan-derived estimates for the same features.
instruments: Preserve original attribution: 6.5-inch overall height was tape-measured; the supplied mm face dimensions were caliper measurements.

separate_installed_tip_readings.method: Straight-line 3D distances between end-face centers at different depths from the wall.
separate_installed_tip_readings.use: Do not use directly as planar CAD hole spacing. Projected tip spacing requires the depth difference; inclined rod axes at the backing plane require separate reconciliation.

preserved_endpoint_meanings.106.39_mm: Gap between nearest mounting-hole edges, not center spacing.
preserved_endpoint_meanings.11.71_mm: Upper-right mounting-hole edge to outside metal rim, not center-to-rim.

engineering_interpretation: Do not discount the inner-plate dimensions using unequal tip depths, average them with a distorted scan, or invent a numerical caliper tolerance. Unknown diameters, inferred center positions, installed registration and physical fit remain separate from confidence in the measured face dimensions.
